inputs.root_cause: validation/validator.py checked arity only for `sizes` (via dimension) and `kinds`, even though SAL-NRRD-00010 (verified, Teem NRRD Format Specification Sections 1.3 and 6) states every baseline per-axis field -- spacings, axis mins, axis maxs, centers, labels, units -- and the later-version fields kinds/thicknesses must each carry exactly one value per declared dimension. NrrdDocument had no typed access to most of these fields at all (only `kinds` existed as a property), so the gap was both missing validation and missing model surface.

execution_steps: 1. Read SAL-NRRD-00010 and its neighbor SAL-NRRD-00009 (labels/units are quote-delimited strings, \" escapes a literal embedded quote, no other escaping) directly from shared/sal-facts/nrrd.yaml before writing anything -- both fact_status: verified, citing the Teem NRRD Format Specification.

2. Confirmed via grep that none of spacings/axis mins/axis maxs/centers/labels/units/thicknesses appeared anywhere in reader.py or document.py by name -- these fields were entirely unmodeled, not merely unvalidated.

3. Added model/document.py: _parse_quoted_list() (a quote-aware tokenizer implementing SAL-NRRD-00009's exact escaping rule -- a naive whitespace split would miscount a label containing an embedded space inside its quotes) plus typed properties spacings/axis_mins/axis_maxs/centers/labels/units/thicknesses, mirroring the existing kinds property's shape. Added per_axis_field_arities(), reporting the declared length of every per-axis field actually present in the header (absent fields are not a violation; only a present field with the wrong count is).
4. Extended validation/validator.py's validate() to check every field per_axis_field_arities() reports against document.dimension, alongside the existing kinds check (left untouched, not duplicated).

5. Wrote tests/python/nrrd/test_obligation_axis_field_arity.py: typed-access tests for all seven new properties including the quote-escaping edge case, positive tests proving correct arity validates across three different dimensions (1, 2, 4) and across the kinds/thicknesses later-version fields, and one negative test per field proving a mismatched count is rejected with a diagnostic naming that field, plus a multi-field-mismatch test proving independent, non-exclusive reporting.

6. First run surfaced a test-construction bug, not a product bug: the fixture builder used a fixed 8-element array/empty payload regardless of the parametrized dimension/sizes, so the dimension-matrix positive tests failed on a pre-existing, unrelated payload-length check rather than on anything this slice added. Fixed by computing the correct element count from sizes and round-tripping the draft through dumps()/loads() so each fixture is a genuinely self-consistent document -- isolates the per-axis-arity assertion from incidental payload-size noise.

7. All 24 new tests passed after the fixture fix. Re-ran the full NRRD suite: 412 passed, 1 pre-existing skip unchanged (388 baseline + 24 new, 0 regressions). ruff and mypy clean on the full package (19 source files).

8. Re-read the obligation's proof_requirements against what was actually built: positive 'All per-axis fields across dimensions and profiles' and negative 'Every per-axis field with mismatched arity' are both now covered -- every baseline and later-version field has both a positive (correct-arity) and negative (mismatched-arity) selector, and the positive side additionally spans three distinct dimensions. missing_behavior for this specific obligation is genuinely empty; promoted to implemented on that basis. Two sibling obligations (SAL-NRRD-OBL-94D8938DE18A6562, NRRD-SHAPE-001, and SAL-NRRD-OBL-2085AD256AFE6E96, NRRD-VALIDATE-001) referenced 'per-axis arities' among their own listed gaps -- updated their missing_behavior text to remove that closed clause while preserving their own remaining, separate gaps (an axis-order model/conversion report, and conditional-field/version-feature/trailing-payload rules respectively). Neither sibling is promoted -- each still has real, distinct missing_behavior of its own.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/nrrd/ -q -- 412 passed, 1 skipped (388 baseline + 24 new, 0 regressions)
.venv/Scripts/python -m ruff check src/python/nrrd/src/format_factory/nrrd/ tests/python/nrrd/test_obligation_axis_field_arity.py -- All checks passed
.venv/Scripts/python -m mypy src/python/nrrd/src/format_factory/nrrd/ -- Success: no issues found in 19 source files

evidence.oracle: none -- this is format_factory's own self-consistent test evidence, not independently verified against Teem or another reference implementation for this specific field set. Labeled SELF-CONSISTENT per the FF6 execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 remediation rule, not VERIFIED; 'implemented' in this ledger's schema means complete, self-consistent, selector-bound proof against the obligation's own declared proof_requirements, which is a narrower claim than independent verification and is not conflated with it here.
evidence.why_only_one_obligation_promoted: SAL-NRRD-OBL-428BE326FCBC9A6E's entire declared gap was per-axis arity validation, now fully closed. Its two siblings under the same rule area (SAL-NRRD-OBL-94D8938DE18A6562 and SAL-NRRD-OBL-2085AD256AFE6E96) each bundle the now-closed arity gap together with a genuinely separate, still-open requirement (an axis-order model/conversion report; conditional-field and version-feature validation) -- promoting them would overclaim, so only their missing_behavior text was corrected, not their status.
